extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — investigators, grant applicants, research administrators, and institutional staff involved in NIH grants
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH updates, resources, and reminders relevant to applicants and awardees in the NIH extramural grants community. Items highlight policy changes, new resources, and process updates applicants should consider when preparing or managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select research models appropriate to questions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Investigators should still select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches, including New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), with an emphasis on approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential. Choose the model(s) that best address the research question rather than selecting a model solely because it is favored or new.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 application format and linked-award handling
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview of the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure to learn key features, application format, and how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants for the PF5 mechanism should review the video/resource to understand the required application format and the possibility that applications may be split into linked awards after peer review and prior to Just-in-Time (JIT) requests — plan proposals and budgets accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plans."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans, use the 2026 pilot format and include the specified required elements. This is a simplified set intended for pilot use; consult the full guidance/resource for exact element list and formatting expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility throughout research
rubrics_metrics.description: "The reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust in science and to ensuring that findings can benefit patients and communities. NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan advances this commitment by encouraging a culture that values replication and reproducibility."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and awardees should incorporate replication and reproducibility considerations into their study designs, methods, and research plans. NIH has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts; consider how proposals align with this highlighted topic and related expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of 'competitive but not discussed' scoring implications
rubrics_metrics.description: "My Application Was Scored as 'Competitive But Not Discussed' During Review. What Does This Mean?" — NIH implemented emergency modifications designating the middle third of applications in a study section as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should understand that being scored as 'competitive but not discussed' may result from review-process cutoffs and does not necessarily mean the application is weak. Monitor NIH notices about review modifications and implications for resubmission, summary statements, and funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect centralized peer review under CSR and related effects
rubrics_metrics.description: "In March 2025, NIH announced that all peer review would be centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR)... As the one-year anniversary approaches, we are providing an update on the consolidation and its initial effects on the peer-review process."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and institutions should anticipate procedural and possibly substantive changes associated with centralized review (e.g., efficiency, competition, transparency). Stay current with NIH guidance on how centralization affects review timelines, study section assignment, and reviewer processes.
